title: Annotatio II §.IV close: CONCEPTIO error 3 — Bertram/Ratramnus & Berengar; embryo into public light; stop before §.V
pass_a_gloss: There came at length a THIRD error, born under the ninth and eleventh centuries, owed partly to crudely understood utterances of Bertram, otherwise Ratramnus, in the book On the body of Christ to Charles the Bald, on the figure of Christ’s body in the Sacred Supper after the mind of the older Fathers — to be recited entire elsewhere — partly to Berengar’s sayings on the same figure of Christ’s body, taken too crudely, even if not so crudely by him: for very many of those opposing them so denied that the bread is a figure of Christ’s body in the sacred Eucharist that they urged a Corporal Union of this with that, and so made the Consubstantiation embryo hitherto conceived and fostered — whether crasser or subtler — come forth into public light.
pass_b_english: THIRD error (9th–11th c.): crudely heard Bertram/Ratramnus on the figure of Christ’s body (to Charles the Bald), plus Berengar’s figure-sayings taken too raw.
Opponents denied figure so hard they urged corporal union — and so forced the long-fostered Consubstantiation embryo, crass or subtle, into public light.
Stop before §.V (Paschasius Radbertus as alleged first author).
source_text: Accessit tandem TERTIUS error, Seculo nono & undecimo subnatus, ex partim crudè intellectis Bertrami, alias Ratramni, in libro de corpore Christi ad Carol. Calvum, de figura corporis Christi in S. Coena, ad mentem antiquiorum Patrum, enunciatis, alibi recitandis integris; partim crudè nimis, de eadem figura corporis Christi, Berengarii effatis, utut non ita crudè ab ipso acceptis, debitus: His enim sese opponentium plurimi, ita panem corporis Christi figuram negarunt in Eucharistia sacra esse, ut Corporalem hujus cum isto Unionem urserint, sicque conceptum fotumque hactenus Consubstantiationis embryonem, vel crassiorem, vel subtiliorem, in lucem publicam prodire fecerint.
